candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XLII.24. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'And he turned himself about from them, and wept; and returned to them again'. Ephrem treats Joseph's hidden weeping as the model of concealed-compassion: Joseph maintains the testing-disguise BUT the compassion is real and ongoing. Tewahedo pastoral-theology preserves this image: shepherds and confessors may need to maintain apparent severity for the penitent's good, but the compassion underneath must always be active.
